sense.text:
We are talking about the first covenant. “Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.” This is the sanctuary of the Lord, the first of the sanctuaries of the Lord this class goes over.

Many of us grew up without this truth. We grew up in Christianity, in Islam, in various other religions, or with no direction at all. Who read Leviticus in the Christian church? Who read the Bible in the Christian church? We never read Leviticus, so what Paul is going over here in Hebrews is understood from Leviticus, and from the pattern of the tabernacle itself.

“For there was a tabernacle made”: that is what we are looking at in the picture of the tabernacle. “The first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.” Past the first veil is the sanctuary.

The candlestick has seven candlesticks. Not nine: seven. That is what we read in the Bible. Out front of the tabernacle is the laver, where the priest washed and prepared.

“And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all”: there is the first veil, and after that the second veil. Behind it was “the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant.”

“And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat”: what is over the ark is the mercy seat, with the cherubims of glory over it. This is shown in Exodus 25, where the Lord gave Moses the pattern for it.

“Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God.” The priests accomplished the service of God. That service belongs to the Israelites: you don’t see God telling the Jebusites to build him a sanctuary, or telling Israel to build it and then let the Moabites come and worship. He is being very specific, telling the Israelites what to do, and you don’t see it for any other nation in the Bible. It is more proof that God is only dealing with the Israelites, and always has. People are willfully being ignorant.

precepts.why:
“And let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them.” The sanctuary was made so that the Lord could dwell among the children of Israel. So the Lord dwelt among the children of Israel.

It was to be made exactly as he showed it: “According to all that I shew thee, after the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all the instruments thereof, even so shall ye make it.” That is the worldly sanctuary of the first covenant that Hebrews 9 describes.

Because the Lord dwelt among Israel, he went with them. “When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for the Lord thy God is with thee.” That is what it says: the Lord thy God is with thee. Why? Because he is dwelling among us, the God “which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.”

The priest was to approach and speak unto the people: “Hear, O Israel, ye approach this day unto battle against your enemies: let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble, neither be ye terrified because of them.” Why? “For the Lord your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.” So the Lord our God goes with us to fight against our enemies. That is what the sanctuary meant for Israel: the Lord in the midst of them.

This is the mercy seat Hebrews 9:5 speaks of, the thing Paul could not “now speak particularly” of. “And thou shalt make a mercy seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof.” Two cherubims of gold, of beaten work, one on each end of the mercy seat, stretching forth “their wings on high, covering the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces shall look one to another; toward the mercy seat shall the faces of the cherubims be.” That is the picture of the mercy seat.

“And thou shalt put the mercy seat above upon the ark; and in the ark thou shalt put the testimony that I shall give thee.” Then: “And there I will meet with thee.” There the Most High would meet with us: “and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony, of all things which I will give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel.” It is the children of Israel he meets with and gives the commandment to.

Hebrews 9:6 says the priests accomplished the service of God, and Romans 9 says whose service that is. Paul says, “For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh”, and this comes back up later in the class.

Who are his kinsmen? “Who are Israelites.” We are in the New Testament, in the book of Romans, reading about the Israelites: “to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came.” The service of God pertains to the Israelites, and Christ came for the Israelites. It is more proof that God is only dealing with the Israelites.

sense.text:
“But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people.” He went into the second, past the second veil, once a year, not without blood. The errors means the sins of the people. This was the sacrifice of the day of atonement in Leviticus 16 and 23, and the priests were the sons of Aaron.

Why is Paul bringing this out to the Hebrews in the New Testament? Because it is theirs. The question should be why anybody that is not an Israelite is quoting out of the book of Hebrews, why anybody that is not an Israelite is reading the Bible at all. The Lord doesn’t want you touching his Bible.

“The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing.” While the first tabernacle was yet standing, the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest.

“Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect.” The gifts and the sacrifices could not make us perfect, “as pertaining to the conscience.” Isaiah 1 is the example of it: we were bringing sacrifice after sacrifice, and our consciences were not perfect. That is why Christ had to come.

precepts.why:
“And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all.” Then: “For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the Lord.”

This was one of the sacrifices that was done at a particular time, this being the day of atonement. “It shall be a sabbath of rest unto you, and ye shall afflict your souls, by a statute for ever.” That once a year atonement is when the high priest went into the second tabernacle with blood.

“Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.” No work was to be done that day, “for it is a day of atonement, to make an atonement for you before the Lord your God.”

“For whatsoever soul it be that shall not be afflicted in that same day, he shall be cut off from among his people.” The Lord will kill him. “The same soul will I destroy from among his people”: the same soul will God destroy from among his people.

“And he shall make an atonement for the holy sanctuary, and he shall make an atonement for the tabernacle of the congregation, and for the altar, and he shall make an atonement for the priests, and for all the people of the congregation.”

“And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you, to make an atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year.” This was the sacrifice made when the priest went past the second veil once a year, the priests being the sons of Aaron, and it was made for the children of Israel.

sense.text: This is the example of Hebrews 9:9, gifts and sacrifices that could not make the one that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience. “To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the Lord: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.”

“When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts?” He said to tread my courts, because we were just bringing sacrifice after sacrifice. Our consciences weren’t perfect. The sacrifice was to discipline us so that we wouldn’t continue to commit the sins, and we kept committing them. This is why our minds weren’t perfect, and this is why Christ had to come.

“Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; the new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with.” “Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth.”

Christianity uses Isaiah 1 to say we shouldn’t be keeping the feasts and the new moons, to say God is not happy with us keeping them. It is not saying don’t do it. It is saying don’t do it in vain: do it with joyfulness and gladness of heart, and don’t keep doing it while committing the same sins. Some of us do the same today, coming with a long face to the new moon when we didn’t really want to be here. Paul and Christ are all in the New Testament still keeping the feasts. And why would we have to stop doing it now when we are going to have to do it in the Kingdom? We are rehearsing the righteous acts.

A rehearsal is practice for a later performance. Christians out there are saying rehearse doesn’t mean that anymore. Like what the hell is it? Rehearse means to practice something over and over, like we are doing: we are rehearsing the righteous acts by keeping these commandments, keeping the feasts and the new moons, for the later performance of keeping the feast of tabernacles in the Kingdom.

“And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.” The Lord says, I’m not listening, because your hands are full of blood.

precepts.why:
This shows the mindset we had when we were sacrificing. “He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog’s neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swine’s blood.” We know the swine is unclean. That is the mindset that we had: we did not give the care and diligence to the Lord’s sacrifices. “He that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol.”

“Yea, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations.” The Lord said they have chosen their own way. So “I also will choose their delusions, and will bring their fears upon them; because when I called, none did answer; when I spake, they did not hear: but they did evil before mine eyes, and chose that in which I delighted not.” Mark where it says I also will choose their delusions: 2 Thessalonians 2 is the same spirit.

“And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.” It is the same spirit as Isaiah 66:4. “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie.” White Jesus, God loves everybody, politics. “That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.”

So the delusion God chooses for them comes because they had no love of the truth, and what that truth is, Psalms 119 shows.

For the new people who may not understand what the truth is that they don’t believe, the truth they don’t have the love of: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” So they didn’t have the love of the law. They didn’t delight in the laws of God.

“I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” That is what was missing. They didn’t delight in those things, so when we brought our oblations, our sacrifices, it was just business as usual. That is why the Lord was weary of our sacrifices and new moons in Isaiah 1: not that his law was done away, but that it was not in our hearts.

“For as the new heavens and the new earth”: this tells you the time frame, the new heavens and the new earth, “which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the Lord, so shall your seed and your name remain.” At that time it shall come to pass, “that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” You know that is a future prophecy, because all flesh is not worshiping the Lord in that manner today. So the new moons and the sabbaths of Isaiah 1:13 are not done away with; they will be kept in the Kingdom, and what we keep now is the rehearsal.

“And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me”, the dead bodies, “for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.” That is that damnation, that everlasting fire.

A precept on the sacrifices and offerings of Isaiah 1. He didn’t say don’t do the sacrifice no more; it was the way they were doing it, where their mindset was. It is like a coach whose team comes out unfocused: go back in the locker room, we don’t even need to practice. We do need to practice, but not with the mindset y’all got. That is all the Most High was saying: don’t even bring nothing in here; you got to change your mind.

“A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master: if then I be a father, where is mine honour?” The Most High was calling them out: you understand this on a basic level of respect and honor for your elders, and I’m the father of all flesh, where is my honour? “And if I be a master, where is my fear?” Where is the fear you have for your master? “Saith the Lord of hosts unto you, O priests, that despise my name.” The priests, the same as was gone over in Leviticus: they were defiling the offerings in the way they went before the Lord.

“Ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar.” That was the problem: the offerings they were bringing were polluted, not up to the standard he told them to bring forth. “In that ye say, The table of the Lord is contemptible.” How was it contemptible? “And if ye offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? and if ye offer the lame and sick, is it not evil?” The lamb was supposed to be without spot or blemish. If you got a blind lamb, is that what you are supposed to be offering to the Lord? No.

“Offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or accept thy person? saith the Lord of hosts.” Take that same offering to the governor, since you don’t want to reverence me, and see how he deals with it. So he was challenging them. It wasn’t that the day was to be done away with, or that the day was evil; it was the manner in which they were revering and honoring it, and the way in which we reverenced it made it evil.

Backing up that precept from Malachi: “And he said unto Aaron, Take thee a young calf for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering, without blemish”. Without blemish: that is just what Malachi was talking about. “And offer them before the Lord.”

“And unto the children of Israel thou shalt speak, saying, Take ye a kid of the goats for a sin offering; and a calf and a lamb, both of the first year, without blemish, for a burnt offering.” Without blemish again. The law commanded offerings without blemish, and Israel brought the blind, the lame and the sick. That smashes the doctrine that Isaiah 1 does away with the feasts: the Lord rejected the vain and polluted offerings, not his own ordinances.

sense.text: Back to Hebrews to smash that doctrine, because that’s what we be about: smashing doctrines. The tabernacle and its service “was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience”. The sacrifices could not make the one offering them perfect, and the perfection it speaks of is the conscience.

precepts.why:
Jump over to chapter 10: “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.” Those that came to offer those sacrifices were not made perfect by them. Perfect how? As according to the conscience, the same thing Hebrews 9:9 said.

“For then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins. But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.” And “it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.” It was not possible for those sacrifices to take away sins.

“Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure. Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.”

“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first”: he taketh away the first covenant, “that he may establish the second. By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.”

So those sacrifices were offered by the law, that law given to Moses, and they were a figure that could not perfect the conscience. Christ’s body, offered once for all, is what sanctifies.

sense.text: “Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me”. That’s what to deal with: “when he cometh into the world.” Who did Christ come into the world for, and whose sin did he take away? The prevailing thought is that Jesus came for everybody. That’s the doctrine that’s been preached and pushed throughout the earth, and the scriptures say otherwise.

precepts.why:
When he cometh into the world: “He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not. He came unto his own, and his own received him not.”

A lot of Christians get hung up on that. They say everybody rejected Christ. That’s not true.

“He came unto his own, and his own received him not”: what is that? “And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.” Rejected of who? Of the elders, the chief priests and the scribes. It was the leaders that rejected him, not everybody.

“The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” Behold what? The Lamb of God. Which taketh away the sin of the world: the sin of those who God called to sacrifice, to make it plain.

We’re talking about sacrifice: “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” We are reading about those sacrifices. Who made a covenant with the Lord by sacrifice? The Israelites. So the Lamb of God that takes away the sin of the world takes away the sin of the people that were in covenant with the Lord by sacrifice.

Read John 1:29-31 again with that cleared up, so it makes more sense, because the prevailing thought is that Jesus came for everybody. “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” Then John says, “And I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water.” That he should be what? Manifest to Israel. Christ came for Israel.

“Then Pilate entered into the judgment hall again, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Art thou the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “Sayest thou this thing of thyself, or did others tell it thee of me?” Christ asked him: did you know this of yourself, or did other people tell you?

“Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Thine own nation and the chief priests have delivered thee unto me: what hast thou done?” Read that part again: thine own nation and the chief priests. Pilate says, am I a Jew?

“Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence.” “Pilate therefore said unto him, Art thou a king then?” Are you king of the Jews?

“Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a king. To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.” That’s the point: “Every one that is of the truth”. Everyone that is of the truth is going to hear the words of this Bible. They’re not going to be scoffing at the word.

“My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.” Every one that is of the truth heareth his voice, and those are his sheep.

sense.text:
“Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.” That time of reformation is the time of Christ.

That establishes the sanctuary and the sacrifices, and who they belong to: who those sacrifices that were performed in the sanctuary belong to.

Switching gears to Ezekiel. “Moreover the spirit lifted me up, and brought me unto the east gate of the Lord’s house, which looketh eastward: and behold at the door of the gate five and twenty men; among whom I saw Jaazaniah the son of Azur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people.”

“Then said he unto me, Son of man, these are the men that devise mischief, and give wicked counsel in this city”. These are the men that devise mischief and give wicked counsel in the city, and chapter 8 shows what was going on among them.

“Son of man, seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? but turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations.”

“And behold every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” These abominable beasts were portrayed round about on the walls. This is what we grew up with on the walls. This is what we grew up with in the churches, on the stained glass.

“And there stood before them seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel, and in the midst of them stood Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan, with every man his censer in his hand; and a thick cloud of incense went up.” Hold on: that Jaazaniah. Go back and read Ezekiel 11:1 again, where at the east gate stood Jaazaniah the son of Azur, and set the two side by side.

“Hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” They said the Lord doesn’t see us.
“Behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.” So women were in the midst of idolatry as well.

“Were about five and twenty men, with their backs toward the temple of the Lord, and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun”. They did what? They worshipped the sun. There was all types of idolatry, a bunch of idolatry going on: they were worshipping different images and idols, the women were worshipping Tammuz, and they were worshipping the sun, the moon and the stars.

precepts.why:
“Lest ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female, The likeness of any beast that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged fowl that flieth in the air, The likeness of any thing that creepeth on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the waters beneath the earth”.

“And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them”. Shouldest be what? Driven to worship them, “and serve them, which the Lord thy God hath divided unto all nations under the whole heaven.”

So it’s not the images, it’s the worshipping of the images. That was to set the tone: there was a lot of idolatry going on at that time, the very things the Lord warned against in Deuteronomy 4, and the house of Israel was doing them in the Lord’s house.

sense.text: Back to Ezekiel 11. “Ye have feared the sword; and I will bring a sword upon you, saith the Lord God. And I will bring you out of the midst thereof, and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute judgments among you. Ye shall fall by the sword; I will judge you in the border of Israel”.
“For ye have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my judgments, but have done after the manners of the heathen that are round about you.” Have done what? After the manners of the heathen.

“Son of man, thy brethren, even thy brethren, the men of thy kindred, and all the house of Israel wholly”. Read that part again: thy brethren, even thy brethren, the men of thy kindred. They are the ones to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said, “Get you far from the Lord: unto us is this land given in possession.”

“Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord God; Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” Deal first with this: “Although I have cast them far off among the heathen.” How were we scattered? Into a little history: we were scattered first through the sub-Saharan slave trade, and then through the transatlantic slave trade.

precepts.why: “Although I have cast them far off among the heathen”: “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” That is the scattering Ezekiel 11:16 speaks of.

The sub-Saharan slave trade, with the Arab pictures up: “Lift up thine eyes unto the high places, and see where thou hast not been lien with. In the ways hast thou sat for them, as the Arabian in the wilderness”. As what? As the Arabian in the wilderness. Because we sat for the Arabians, we learned the ways of the Arabians. That’s why when we came over on slave ships there were those of us that were practicing Islam.

Then the transatlantic slave trade: “And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies”. We shall be what? Sold unto your enemies, “for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.” We would be sold unto our enemies for slave men and slave women, and no man would buy us: no one would redeem us out of our condition. Even to this very day we have not had anyone that was able to redeem us out of our conditions.

The papal bull of Pope Nicholas recognized Portugal’s right to the territories it had discovered along the West African coast, where people were already at, and to the reduction of the infidels and non-Christians to perpetual vassals. What is that reduction of infidels referring to? It’s referring to us. Basically they were saying that anybody we come across, we’re going to make slaves. One article uses nice words; the other says it plainly.

Who gave them that right to lands and people? Who said, hey, you can rule over all people? Converting and enslaving: how do you enslave and convert? Those ain’t two of the same thing. When we go to camp we go to convert people; we don’t say, you believe in Jesus? All right, cool, I got a plantation for you. That’s what Esau do.

Colonization paired with race-based slavery. They always say, well, everybody’s been in slavery. No: the slavery they had in the past, I owe you, you owe me, that’s fine, we read about that in the scriptures. It’s never been a whole agenda to put a nation of people in servitude forever. Captives forcibly baptized before being sent to a life of enslavement: that’s forced conversion, and now we do it willingly. That’s the beginning of the transatlantic slave trade.

sense.text:
“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed”. Let no man deceive you. The Israelites would have to fall away from all understanding of who we are. Then see some of the things that would happen to us once we fell away from who we are.

The falling away first: we just read the forced baptism, the forced conversion to Christianity. Look at the different religions that a lot of our people today are still under, on the chart. These are the ones that will scoff at the word when it comes out.

The father of hermeneutics: who pushes hermeneutics more than the black man? We didn’t know what hermeneutics was until we got on Clubhouse. The white man has had it since 1800-something, but it wasn’t until the black man got a hold of it that we knew about it, because he’ll take the white man’s doctrine and spread it throughout the four corners of the earth like it’s the glorious gospel.

The Baptist religion, Mormonism, the Seventh-day Adventists, the Jehovah’s Witnesses, the Pentecostal religion: all made by men. Down in Florida a lot of the brothers from the islands, Levi and Benjamin, are caught up in one or the other, Seventh-day Adventist or Jehovah’s Witness. It’s like Esau be waiting at the docks to pick them off. And how many black people are Pentecostal?

“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods”: there we should serve other gods, “which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Our forefathers didn’t know about any of these gods.

This is one of the curses that goes with the white man religion chart: the Baptist religion, Mormonism, Seventh-day Adventist, Jehovah Witnesses, the Pentecostal religion. Falling away from who we are and coming into these religions is actually a curse. These are the religions a lot of our people are still under today, and these are the ones that will scoff at the word when it comes out.

Down in Florida a lot of the brothers from the islands, Levi and Benjamin, are caught up in one or the other, Seventh-day Adventist or Jehovah Witness. It’s like Esau be waiting at the docks to pick them off. And nobody ever complains about this chart. They’ll complain about the 12 tribes chart, but nobody ever came up and said they don’t like the white man religion chart.

precepts.why:
“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.”

The curses come for not hearkening to the commandments and statutes. Serving other gods in the lands we were scattered to, the religions that were forced on us and that we now keep willingly, is one of those curses that overtook us.

sense.text:
Now we are dealing with the falling away: what else would happen to us when we fell away. We lost all sense of who we are, our nationality, our land, our language, our God, and the Lord said we would be brought down very low. Even in our land we were worshipping other gods, and the Lord said he would judge us for that.

“Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”: noble here is fine personal qualities and high moral values. That was us in our noble state. “How then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” Degenerate is the immoral, corrupt person, showing evidence of decline. This is the falling away: the Lord doesn’t even recognize it. He said, how have you turned into a degenerate plant? You have become strange unto me.

The interview videos show it. On the surface y’all laugh, but this is the result of bad parenting, the result of moral decline, and of the school systems. Remember when Trump said your school systems ain’t crap, you live in the worst places, you get the worst food, what do you got to lose? Esau sits there and keeps them talking to make sport of us, a mockery of our people, and while things are going on in the world our people are tuned in to gossip and foolishness and not seeing Russia and China teaming up together. That is us in a degenerate state.

precepts.why:
“Behold, I have taught you statutes and judgments, even as the Lord my God commanded me, that ye should do so in the land whither ye go to possess it. Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.”

That is the noble vine: a people with high moral values, keeping the statutes and judgments, so that the nations would call us a great nation and a wise and understanding people. That would be us in our nobility, before we were turned into the degenerate plant.

There shall be no … of the daughters of Israel, “nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.” We should not have whoredom in the land.

We have single mothers, and she better not have no husband at home letting somebody push up on her like that. This is us in our degenerate state.

Next is the LGBTQ: this is us in our degenerate state. “Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections”: God gave them up to vile affections.

“For even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: and likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman”, “men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.”

Again, this is how we came down into a degenerate state, the falling away, us becoming very low. A father watches over his daughter “In her virginity, lest she should be defiled and gotten with child in her father’s house; and having an husband, lest she should misbehave herself; and when she is married, lest she should be barren.”

So when you come home pregnant without a husband in your father’s house, the Bible says you are defiled.

“The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart: and thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore.”

Madness is extreme foolishness, and this is the drugs. When you put drugs into your body: if you’ve seen what some of these drugs do to the masses of people. They got drugs out here now that you take and it literally will eat your skin, it starts to make your skin dissolve, and when you hit it once you’re hooked.

Again, this is us fallen in our low estate, degenerate, defiling our bodies. “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.”

Putting drugs into the body defiles the temple of God, and him shall God destroy.

“What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?” Ye are not your own. “For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” Our bodies are not ours to defile; they belong to God.

This is the scripture about your body being lent. The idol maker “maketh a vain god of the same clay, even he which a little before was made of earth himself, and within a little while after returneth to the same”, “when his life which was lent him shall be demanded.” Our life was lent to us, and it will be demanded back, so we are not to destroy the body we were given.

Again, this is us falling, and here is the prison. “But this is a people robbed and spoiled; they are all of them snared in holes”: we are snared in holes. “And they are hid in prison houses”: we are hid in prison houses. “They are for a prey, and none delivereth; for a spoil, and none saith, Restore.”

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people”.

When we would fall away they would be able to call us all kinds of byewords. They call us Black, African American, Haitian, Dominican, Jamaican, Puerto Rican, El Salvadorian, Ecuadorian, Trinidadian. This is us falling away, losing our identity. That’s not what God called us.

sense.text:
Now with all of this that has come upon us, let’s see what the Lord said. “Behold ye among the heathen, and regard, and wonder marvellously: for I will work a work in your days, which ye will not believe, though it be told you.” The Lord would still work a work in our days, waking us up even from this low estate, and it would be marvelous in the sight of the nations.

The Lord will work a marvelous work in our time, and you brothers and sisters sitting out there, you that are tuned in, many of you are part of this work, part of this marvelous thing the Lord is doing in waking up the 12 tribes of Israel throughout the four corners of the earth.

This is that trauma. James Byrd Jr. was beaten and urinated on, then chained by his ankles behind a pickup truck and dragged until he died. That’s torture: they dragged him on a country dirt road literally till he fell apart.

“And among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind: and thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life.” And thou shalt have none assurance of thy life: James Byrd didn’t expect to die that day, and he died in a gruesome way.

The officer in Georgia told a white woman at a traffic stop, ‘we only kill black people,’ and they called that de-escalating the situation, telling his own people we only kill black people. He used something they both could relate to and understand: you’re white, there’s nothing to be worried about; now if you were a black person you should be very scared right now. Be afraid, be very afraid. That is having no assurance of thy life.
“And ye shall perish among the heathen, and the land of your enemies shall eat you up.” We are seeing evidence of that as we show these videos and pictures.

“If they shall confess their iniquity”: if we should confess our iniquity, “and the iniquity of their fathers”, and that they “have walked contrary unto me; and that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”.

That’s why we are here, scattered throughout the four corners, and right here is where we got to repent, accept of our punishment, and confess our sins.

“Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.” “And they shall accept of the punishment of their iniquity”: we are supposed to accept the punishment of our iniquity, “because they despised my judgments, and because their soul abhorred my statutes.”

“And yet for all that, when they be in the land of their enemies”: are we in the land of our enemies? Yes. “I will not cast them away.” The Lord said he will not cast us away.

That destroys the teaching that because Israel rejected Jesus he is now open for everybody on planet earth. He is still only for the children of Israel. “Neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly, and to break my covenant with them.”

“But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”: the covenant of our ancestors, “whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the heathen, that I might be their God: I am the Lord.”

precepts.why:
This is confessing our iniquity. “Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions. Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.”

“Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.” We have to acknowledge our transgressions before the Lord, the way Leviticus 26:40 says we must confess.

sense.text: Now that we know we’ve fallen into this deep abyss, we go back to Ezekiel 11:16. “Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” Even though he cast us off into these lands, he would not cast us off from being his people.

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The Lord of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.”

So if the sun, the moon, the stars and the waves of the sea depart from before the Lord, then we are no longer Israelites. But we still see all of those things intact today.

“If heaven above can be measured”: who’s trying to measure the heavens? Esau. “And the foundations of the earth searched out beneath”: he’s trying to search out the foundations of the earth, like the movie Journey to the Center of the Earth, and the sub they took down to the Titanic that got smashed. That’s still going on today; they try to search out everything. Yet “I will also cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done, saith the Lord.” He has not cast us off.

sense.text: “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.” Now the Lord is starting to wake us up.

“If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,)”: Israel sinned, and the Lord was angry and delivered them to the enemy, “so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near.” That is us, carried away into the land of our enemies. Now the Lord is starting to wake us up.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves”: if we shall bethink ourselves, remember that we are the Israelites, “in the land whither they were carried captives”, the land where we were carried captives, and repent.

“And make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned”: we have to acknowledge our sins, that we “have done perversely, we have committed wickedness.” Waking up means remembering who we are and owning what we did.

precepts.why:
Now that we’re waking up, we’re searching, we’re trying to find out who we are. That’s why we need these little sanctuaries scattered throughout the earth: we’ve been in a Christian church, and the Christian church never taught us who we are.

“And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness”: that’s what we were doing in the Christian church. Some of us were in the Christian church and it never resonated with our spirit. I can’t get down with a white guy: what is this image? This doesn’t look like me. I know how I get treated when I leave here, and you’re telling me to worship this image? That’s confusion. That’s Babylon.

“And thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.” No man shall save you.

When we bethink ourselves and start searching, this is where the Lord sends us: “Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls.” We shall find rest for our souls in the old paths. “But they said, We will not walk therein.”

sense.text:
“If ye love me, keep my commandments.” That’s what Christ said. What is so hard about that for the Christian church? They say, well, that’s your own interpretation; how do you interpret that? What interpretation do you need?

If you’re in a committed marriage and you say, ‘If you love me, don’t cheat on me’, and the answer is ‘Well, what do you mean by cheating? That’s your interpretation. Love to me is I can have three to four side chicks, I can do whatever I want’, that’s how you love; that’s not how I love. That’s what Christianity is. It’s nonsense.

Christ will pray the Father, “and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you. I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” The Comforter is given to them that love him and keep his commandments.

precepts.why:
“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.” The Comforter brings all things to your remembrance.

So why is it that in the Christian church, and in the Muslim mosque, our brothers and sisters have not woken up and remembered that they’re the Israelites? We even had a Rastafari brother that wanted to argue with us that our doctrine is wrong, and he was asked one question: how did you get here? Slave ships. Well, that’s how the Israelites got here, brother. The Bible don’t say nothing about Rastafari; that’s how the Israelites got here.

sense.text: Now we’re waking up to the understanding of who we are. “Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”: you’ve got to set your house in order; you’ve got to get yourself in order first. Then “comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption.”

“Let go from thee mortal thoughts, cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weak nature, And set aside the thoughts that are most heavy unto thee, and haste thee to flee from these times.” Waking up to who we are means letting go of the mortal thoughts and putting off the weak nature.
“For yet greater evils than those which thou hast seen happen shall be done hereafter.” The world is going to get worse.

What else do we have to do? “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” Rightly dividing the word of truth lets you know there are a lot of people out there that don’t live up to that standard: a lot of people are dividing the word of God incorrectly. Their breakdowns, their understanding, the hermeneutics, the exegesis, is all incorrect.

precepts.why:
We must rightly divide the word of God. “But the word of the Lord was unto them precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little”. So guess what: when they go to church, they’re getting it precept upon precept, line upon line, “that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.”

A lot of our people are getting it precept upon precept and still fall backward, because they’re not taking the word and rightly dividing the word of truth. On the contrary, they’re being snared and taken with that same Bible: it is not another Bible, the understanding is just different.

sense.text: Now that we’ve awakened, now that we’ve come into the little sanctuaries, it’s time to report for duty. “If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.”

“A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity”. That means we start to learn how to be men, the women start to learn how to be women, and we learn how to start ruling our houses.
“For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?” And “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.”
“Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without”: those that are not in the truth, “lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.”

precepts.why: A quick example of having a good report of them which are without: “And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.” Read it again: a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.

“As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.” Do good unto all men, and especially to your brethren that believe what you believe.

“If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” Live peaceably with all men. That’s why we say we are not a hate group, and we are not affiliated with any other Israelite group.

sense.text:
“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” We didn’t know this when we were in a Christian church. This is understanding that is now starting to come to us in these little sanctuaries that have been set up by the Lord, where the spirit of the Lord is dwelling.

The great city is America, the nation that reigns over the kings of the earth. The dead bodies are the spiritually dead: those that have wandered out of the way of the knowledge of God, his commandments, lying in her street.

It is “spiritually” called Egypt because this isn’t the physical Egypt, but it has the same markings of Egypt, and all twelve tribes are here. Right on the back of the dollar bill you have the pyramid and the all-seeing eye. They built a pyramid in Memphis, an arena where a basketball team plays, and one in Vegas, a hotel. This is spiritual Egypt.

And here the image of our God was crucified: “where also our Lord was crucified” is his image crucified and his message crucified.

precepts.why:
“And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth.” What city, what nation, what country is reigning over the kings of the earth? Is it not America, who has military bases?

Read it again with the picture of the bases up: “which reigneth over the kings of the earth”, because they have power, they have might. These are all the places where America has military bases. But does anybody have military bases here in America? No. That is the great city of Revelation 11:8.

To get the understanding of “their dead bodies”: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” Out of the way of understanding is out of the way of the knowledge of God, which is these commandments. He that wanders out of it shall remain in the congregation of the dead: spiritually dead. Those are the dead bodies lying in the street of the great city.

All twelve tribes are here in spiritual Egypt. “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together”: the northern and southern kingdom oppressed together. “And all that took them captives held them fast; they refused to let them go.” They refuse to let us go. This is a prison house for the Israelites, just as Egypt was.

Straight to the point of “where also our Lord was crucified”: “His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire; And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace; and his voice as the sound of many waters.” So does that image they put up look like a dark man with woolly hair? Absolutely not. This is where our Lord was crucified: his image was crucified, and his message was crucified.

“For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached”: you don’t see the Israelites, you don’t hear the Israelites preaching a blond-haired, blue- and green-eyed, stringy-haired Jesus. You don’t hear us preaching that. “Or if ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received, or another gospel, which ye have not accepted, ye might well bear with him.” That other Jesus is his image crucified in spiritual Egypt.

sense.text: Remember, we are reporting for duty. “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.”

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” That he may please him who hath chosen him: because, contrary to popular belief, you didn’t choose the Lord.

precepts.why: A lot of people think that in prison they found Jesus, or when they got divorced they found Jesus, or when they lost their last job they found Jesus. “Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain”. That’s the proof: we didn’t choose the Lord; he chose us, the soldier is chosen by him.

sense.text: The Lord is our example. “For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps”.

“Who did no sin”: that goes back to the sacrifice, blameless, without spot, without blemish. “Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously”.

“Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.” We were dead in sins, and the law is what shows sin: you can’t sin if there’s no law, and the law was given to Israel.
“For ye were as sheep going astray”: we were as sheep going astray, “but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.” Now we are returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of our souls.

precepts.why:
“And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”.

“Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others. But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ”. Even when we were dead in sins: that is the being dead to sins of 1 Peter 2:24, and Christ quickened us out of it.

Even when we were dead in sins: you can’t sin if there’s no law. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.” The law was given to Israel only, so it is Israel that was dead in sins and Israel whose sins he bare.

sense.text: What is the conclusion of the matter? “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” We present our bodies a living sacrifice.

“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” So we have to renounce corruption, we have to overcome our sins, we have to become perfect. That’s what that’s saying: we have to become perfect and acceptable for the Lord.

precepts.why: “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” This is the perfect will of God that we are to prove: to become perfect and acceptable for the Lord.

sense.text: “Be ready to the reward of the kingdom, for the everlasting light shall shine upon you for evermore.” That’s the message: be ready for the reward of the kingdom. That’s our reward for fleeing this world.
“Flee the shadow of this world, receive the joyfulness of your glory: I testify my Saviour openly. O receive the gift that is given you, and be glad”. The ones given that gift are the called.

“Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of the Lord; Which are departed from the shadow of the world”: departed from the shadow of this world, “and have received glorious garments of the Lord.”

“Take thy number, O Sion, and shut up those of thine that are clothed in white, which have fulfilled the law of the Lord.” “The number of thy children, whom thou longedst for, is fulfilled”, “thy people, which have been called from the beginning”. Then “I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs.”

“And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns”. Upon every one of their heads he set crowns: that is the glorious kingdom and the beautiful crown from the Lord’s hand.

“These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of God: now are they crowned, and receive palms.” They put off the mortal and put on the immortal, and they confessed the name of God.

The young person that crowneth them “is the Son of God, whom they have confessed in the world.” “Then began I greatly to commend them that stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord.” They stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord.
“Go thy way, and tell my people what manner of things, and how great wonders of the Lord thy God, thou hast seen.”

precepts.why: Who are the called that are brought to the heavenly kingdom? “Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called; I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.” Jacob and Israel are the called, the same “people, which have been called from the beginning” in 2 Esdras 2:41.

“But the righteous live for evermore”: the righteous live for evermore. “Their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High. Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the Lord’s hand”: that’s what we’re reading in 2 Esdras, the crowns set upon every one of their heads, and the reward of the kingdom. “For with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.”
